title: Adding August reduced mean flow timing correlation at three Arctic gauges in 31 certified years from 1980 to 2011
abstract: We tested the effect of adding August to a spring flow timing window at three Arctic gauges. We used 31 common complete certified years in 1980-2011 from ArcticGRO v20261104. After local linear trend removal, the mean of three pair correlations fell from 0.231 for April-July to 0.064 for April-August. The paired difference was -0.167, with conditional 95% five-year block limits of -0.335 to -0.010. Three- and seven-year blocks retained negative limits. A fixed August-to-spring volume ratio gave a mean correlation of 0.198. The actual extended mean was 0.134 lower than this control, with limits of -0.261 to -0.022. An exact quantile identity links the metric to the added flow share. The shorter 1980-1999 sample gave uncertain decreases. This extends a prior campaign signal with paired uncertainty and a metric diagnostic on the same data. It does not prove a physical cause or coastal effect. Short records, regulation, source error and conditional resampling limit inference. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, an independent arithmetic audit and a figure are included.

display.caption: Mean timing correlations and paired contrasts at three Arctic gauges. Limits use joint five-year residual blocks and are conditional on fixed trends and median ratios.
